description:
Hey, I need help triaging some incidents from our monitoring system. I've got a JSON file at `/home/user/incidents/raw_incidents.json` that contains an array of incident objects. I need you to extract all **critical or high severity** incidents that are currently **open** (not resolved), and write them to a CSV file for the on-call team.

Each incident object in the JSON has these fields:
- `id`: string, e.g. "INC-001"
- `title`: string, a short description
- `severity`: string, one of "critical", "high", "medium", "low"
- `status`: string, one of "open", "resolved", "investigating"
- `service`: string, the affected service name
- `opened_at`: string, ISO 8601 timestamp e.g. "2024-11-01T08:23:00Z"

Please write the filtered and sorted results to `/home/user/incidents/triage.csv`.

The CSV must have exactly this header line:
```
id,severity,service,title,opened_at
```

Include only rows where `severity` is `"critical"` or `"high"` AND `status` is `"open"` OR `"investigating"` (i.e. exclude any incident that is fully `"resolved"`). So include open + investigating incidents with critical or high severity.

Sort the output rows by severity first (all `critical` rows before all `high` rows), then within the same severity sort by `opened_at` ascending (oldest first).

Each row should have exactly those five fields in that column order. If the `title` field contains a comma, it must be wrapped in double quotes.

The file should have no trailing newline after the last data row — just a final newline character ending that last row (standard Unix line endings).

Do not include any incidents with `severity` of `"medium"` or `"low"`, and do not include any incidents where `status` is `"resolved"`.
truth:

  {"id":"INC-003","title":"API gateway returning 503 errors","severity":"critical","status":"investigating","service":"api-gateway","opened_at":"2024-11-01T07:55:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-004","title":"Disk usage above 90 percent","severity":"medium","status":"open","service":"filestore","opened_at":"2024-11-01T10:00:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-005","title":"Payment service latency spike","severity":"high","status":"open","service":"payments","opened_at":"2024-11-01T09:45:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-006","title":"SSL certificate expiring soon","severity":"low","status":"open","service":"nginx","opened_at":"2024-11-01T11:00:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-007","title":"Auth service, token validation failing","severity":"critical","status":"open","service":"auth","opened_at":"2024-11-01T08:05:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-008","title":"Search index out of sync","severity":"high","status":"investigating","service":"search","opened_at":"2024-11-01T08:50:00Z"},
  {"id":"INC-009","title":"Batch job failure in ETL pipeline","severity":"high","status":"resolved","service":"etl","opened_at":"2024-11-01T07:30:00Z"},

]

Expected file `/home/user/incidents/triage.csv`:
id,severity,service,title,opened_at
INC-003,critical,api-gateway,API gateway returning 503 errors,2024-11-01T07:55:00Z
INC-007,critical,auth,"Auth service, token validation failing",2024-11-01T08:05:00Z
INC-001,critical,postgres,Database connection pool exhausted,2024-11-01T08:23:00Z
INC-010,critical,storage,Object storage bucket unreachable,2024-11-01T09:00:00Z
INC-008,high,search,Search index out of sync,2024-11-01T08:50:00Z
INC-005,high,payments,Payment service latency spike,2024-11-01T09:45:00Z

Filtering logic:
- Excluded: INC-002 (high+resolved), INC-004 (medium), INC-006 (low), INC-009 (high+resolved)
- Included critical+non-resolved: INC-001(open), INC-003(investigating), INC-007(open), INC-010(open)
- Included high+non-resolved: INC-005(open), INC-008(investigating)
- Sort: critical first by opened_at asc: INC-003(07:55), INC-007(08:05), INC-001(08:23), INC-010(09:00); then high by opened_at asc: INC-008(08:50), INC-005(09:45)
- INC-007 title contains a comma, so it must be quoted in CSV.

The file has 7 lines total (1 header + 6 data rows), each ending with \n.
